subject: Deal orchestration: token throttle playbook & SLA triggers
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@meridian.ai>, ops@meridian.ai
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deal orchestration: token throttle playbook & SLA triggers

Laura / Meridian ops team —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is a first-pass operational playbook and a tokens/sec model for the pilot (see meridian_token_model_v2.xlsx). High-level ask: we need to land a pragmatic dedicated-capacity plan that meets the p95 SLO for interactive completion paths while keeping committed GPU slabs reasonable for Q4.

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Model variant: redwood-ic-13b (int8 inference path).
- Typical completion length: 120 tokens (median), 450 tokens (95th).
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 220 ms for user-facing completions.
- Expected steady-state TPS (request rate): 35 reqs/s, token mix ~ 60% short prompts, 40% long.

Preliminary numbers from our runtime sim (sheet: "token_curve"):
- Nominal throughput (no-headroom): ~9,200 tokens/sec across a 1-slab pool (A100-equivalent slot) with continuous batching and KV warm.
- Tail cases (cold KV / model warm start): effective tokens/sec drops to ~6,200 for first-minute spikes.
- Recommended headroom: 20–30% for burst absorption + operational safety.

Questions for you before we finalize slab asks:
1) Do you expect >25% of traffic to be long completions (>300 tokens) during peak hours?
2) Any quiet-hours/off-peak throttling we can assume for lower-tier endpoints?
3) Are you OK with a two-slab commit (1 active + 1 burst) vs a 3-slab commit for guaranteed p95?

Next steps: Kimberly and Karthik will run a short sensitivity sweep (quantization vs batching) and propose the conservative slab count and the graceful-degrade policy (how we throttle/queue).

Attachments: meridian_token_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, summary + scenario tabs)

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura@meridian.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Meridian.ai Ops <ops@meridian.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal orchestration: token throttle playbook & SLA triggers

Connor — thanks for the summary and the sheet. Quick clarifications: we ran a small pilot last month with a different checkpoint and saw a higher tail for long completions. A few specifics from our side:
- Peak window is M-F 09:00-12:00 PT, and yes, we see up to 35% long completions in that interval (primarily from analyst workflows).
- We have a soft throttling knob in our app for non-interactive batch jobs, but we'd prefer not to throttle analyst interactive completions.
- Cold-warm behavior: our traffic has occasional cold bursts after deploys and when restarting workers (we can push a deploy freeze into the pilot window if needed).

Can you call out the trade-offs between committing 2 slabs vs 3 slabs in plain language? Also curious on the quantization recommendations — we have compliance questions about 4-bit weights.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of ML Platform, Meridian.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@meridian.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-27T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal orchestration: token throttle playbook & SLA triggers

Laura — thanks for the detail. I ran three sensitivity scenarios against the spreadsheet Connor shared and pasted the headroom math below (condensed):

Quoted previous:
> - Nominal throughput (no-headroom): ~9,200 tokens/sec across a 1-slab pool
> - Tail cases (cold KV / model warm start): effective tokens/sec drops to ~6,200

My results (assumes A100-equivalent slab; redwood-ic-13b int8 profile):
- Scenario A (2-slab commit: active + burst, conservative batching):
  - Steady tokens/sec capacity: 18,000 (2 slabs * 9,200)
  - Effective tail capacity when cold: 12,400 (2 * 6,200)
  - Modeled demand peak (our blended mix): ~14,500 tokens/sec
  - Result: 2 slabs insufficient for p95 if cold starts coincide with peak (shortfall ~2,100 tokens/sec).

- Scenario B (3-slab commit: 2 active + 1 burst):
  - Steady capacity: 27,600 tokens/sec
  - Tail cold capacity: 18,600 tokens/sec
  - Result: meets modeled demand with ~28% headroom on steady and ~28% headroom on cold tail.

- Scenario C (2-slab + aggressive quantization & batching):
  - If you allow int8->4-bit (with validation) and increase average batch size from 8->14 for interactive routes, per-slab nominal tokens/sec can rise ~45% to ~13,300.
  - Effective 2-slab steady capacity becomes ~26,600 tokens/sec; cold tail capacity roughly ~18,000 tokens/sec (with warm-cache assumptions).
  - Result: 2 slabs + 4-bit path performs similarly to 3-slab int8 in terms of capacity, but it adds a model validation/regression risk vector.

Practical recommendation:
- For the pilot, commit to 3 slabs for Q4 launch to ensure p95 SLAs even with cold bursts and without touching quantization.
- Run a parallel optimization track: validate 4-bit candidate on a subset of traffic (A/B) and measure user-visible quality delta; if negligible, migrate the burst slab to quantized variant in month 2 to reduce committed cost.

Operational/degrade policy (short form):
1) Primary: favor graceful queuing for non-interactive requests (batch jobs flagged).
2) Secondary: for interactive flows, apply very short (50–100 ms) incremental delays before rejecting to keep p95 within target.
3) Last resort: fallback to a smaller model (redwood-ic-6b) for best-effort completions when both slabs saturate; tag responses so we can track quality impact.

Attachments I uploaded to the shared Drive: meridian_ops_runbook.pdf (ops steps, rollback, alerts), and I updated the spreadsheet with scenario tabs (added: "batch14_quant4" tab).

—Kimberly
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deal orchestration: token throttle playbook & SLA triggers

Perfect — that helps a lot.

Action items:
- Laura: can you confirm whether we can do a deploy freeze during pilot peak (tomorrow 09:00-12:00 PT)? Reply ok/no-ok and we will plan accordingly.
- Meridian ops: please grant the Redwood team validator access to a 10% shadow stream so we can run the 4-bit A/B safely. (Drive link + HS-54783 has details).
- Redwood (Kimberly & Karthik): please produce a final recommended commit (2 vs 3 slabs) and a rollback checklist by EOD Friday.

I'll put these in a short mutual action plan and send a calendar invite after Laura confirms the freeze.

—Connor
